landmarks.name: Alofi Village
landmarks.writeup: The capital of Niue, known for its colonial architecture and local markets.

landmarks.name: Talava Arches
landmarks.writeup: Natural limestone arches located on the southeastern coast, popular for scenic views.

landmarks.name: Limu Pools
landmarks.writeup: Natural rock pools ideal for swimming and snorkeling.

landmarks.name: Hikulagi Sculpture Park
landmarks.writeup: An outdoor park featuring sculptures made from recycled materials, promoting environmental awareness.

head_of_state: King Charles III (represented by the Governor-General of New Zealand)

cultural_events.name: Niue National Day
cultural_events.writeup: Celebrated on October 19th, marking Niue's self-governing status in free association with New Zealand.

cultural_events.name: Village Fiafia Nights
cultural_events.writeup: Weekly cultural events featuring traditional music, dance, and food.

food_writeup: Niuean cuisine features seafood, taro, coconut, and tropical fruits, with traditional dishes like 'umu' (earth oven cooked food) being central to local meals.
brief_history: Niue was settled by Polynesians around 900 AD. It became a British protectorate in 1900 and was annexed by New Zealand in 1901. Niue gained self-governing status in free association with New Zealand in 1974.
current_conflicts: Niue is currently peaceful with no known internal or external conflicts.
